import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Set style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Data preparation
# Clean breed names by taking only the first breed when multiple exist
df['PrimaryBreed'] = df['Rasse1Text'].str.split('/').str[0].str.split(',').str[0].str.strip()

# Get top 10 breeds by count
top_breeds = df['PrimaryBreed'].value_counts().head(10).index.tolist()
df_top_breeds = df[df['PrimaryBreed'].isin(top_breeds)]

# Create figure with subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(18, 12))
fig.suptitle('Zurich Dog Registration Analysis', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', y=0.98)

# Subplot 1: Top 10 dog breeds
ax1 = plt.subplot(2, 2, 1)
breed_counts = df['PrimaryBreed'].value_counts().head(10)
bars = ax1.barh(range(len(breed_counts)), breed_counts.values)
ax1.set_yticks(range(len(breed_counts)))
ax1.set_yticklabels(breed_counts.index, fontsize=9)
ax1.invert_yaxis()
ax1.set_xlabel('Number of Registered Dogs', fontsize=10)
ax1.set_title('Top 10 Most Registered Dog Breeds', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax1.grid(axis='x', alpha=0.3)

# Add count labels to bars
for i, (bar, count) in enumerate(zip(bars, breed_counts.values)):
    ax1.text(count + count*0.01, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2, 
             f'{count:,}', va='center', fontsize=9)

# Subplot 2: Dog age distribution
ax2 = plt.subplot(2, 2, 2)
age_order = sorted(df['AlterVHundLang'].dropna().unique(), 
                   key=lambda x: int(x.split('-')[0]) if '-' in x else int(x.split()[0]))
age_counts = df['AlterVHundLang'].value_counts().reindex(age_order)
bars2 = ax2.bar(range(len(age_counts)), age_counts.values)
ax2.set_xticks(range(len(age_counts)))
ax2.set_xticklabels(age_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right', fontsize=9)
ax2.set_xlabel('Dog Age Group', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_ylabel('Count', fontsize=10)
ax2.set_title('Distribution of Dogs by Age Group', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax2.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3)

# Subplot 3: Dog gender distribution
ax3 = plt.subplot(2, 2, 3)
gender_counts = df['SexHundLang'].value_counts()
colors = ['#FF6B6B', '#4ECDC4']
wedges, texts, autotexts = ax3.pie(gender_counts.values, labels=gender_counts.index, 
                                   autopct='%1.1f%%', startangle=90, colors=colors)
for autotext in autotexts:
    autotext.set_color('white')
    autotext.set_fontweight('bold')
ax3.set_title('Dog Gender Distribution', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Subplot 4: Registration trends by year
ax4 = plt.subplot(2, 2, 4)
year_counts = df['StichtagDatJahr'].value_counts().sort_index()
ax4.plot(year_counts.index, year_counts.values, marker='o', linewidth=2.5, markersize=8)
ax4.set_xlabel('Year', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_ylabel('Number of Registrations', fontsize=10)
ax4.set_title('Dog Registration Trends Over Time', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
ax4.grid(True, alpha=0.3)
ax4.set_xticks(year_counts.index)
ax4.tick_params(axis='x', rotation=45)

# Add value labels to the line plot
for x, y in zip(year_counts.index, year_counts.values):
    ax4.annotate(f'{y:,}', (x, y), textcoords="offset points", 
                 xytext=(0,10), ha='center', fontsize=9)

# Adjust layout and save
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96])
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150, facecolor='white')
plt.close()
